title: Kalenjin Mursik Porridge
author: Mama Wanjiru

heritage.origin: Rift Valley — Kalenjin community homelands (Nandi, Kipsigis, Tugen, Marakwet)
heritage.history: The Kalenjin are internationally famous for producing the world's greatest long-distance runners. Mursik — fermented milk — is considered central to Kalenjin athletic performance and cultural identity. Mursik porridge combines the probiotic-rich fermented milk with finger millet — the legendary breakfast of Kalenjin athletes for generations.
heritage.modernEvolution: Mursik porridge continues to be the breakfast of choice for many Kalenjin athletes at training camps in the Rift Valley.

desc: Kalenjin Mursik Porridge — finger millet porridge prepared with mursik (fermented milk) instead of water, combining two of the Kalenjin community's most sacred foods. The legendary breakfast of Kenya's great runners.
longDesc: Mursik porridge is the breakfast at training camps in Iten, Eldoret, and across the Kalenjin highlands where Kenya's greatest runners prepare for world records and Olympic medals.
ingredients: 2 cups mursik (see KEN171) or natural yogurt as substitute
steps: Mix millet flour with cold water to a smooth slurry.
Heat the mursik gently in a saucepan — do not boil.
Add the millet slurry to the warm mursik, stirring constantly.
Cook over medium-low heat for 10—12 minutes, stirring continuously, until thick.
Season with honey and a pinch of salt.
chefTips: Do not boil the mursik hard — excessive heat destroys the probiotic bacteria.
Natural yogurt is the best substitute if mursik is unavailable.
cookingScience: Mursik's lactic acid bacteria survive brief warming but are destroyed by boiling. The combination of complete dairy protein and plant-based iron and calcium creates a particularly nutritionally synergistic meal.
sustainabilityTips: Mursik is prepared from locally herded cattle milk — a sustainable, community-based food system.
healthBenefits: Low glycaemic index for sustained athletic energy.
culturalNote: Mursik porridge is the breakfast of champions — literally. Every marathon world record holder from Kenya has grown up eating this.
